Banks remain well capitalized, with regulatory capital exceeding the 12 percent prudential requirement, reaching a 19 percent regulatory capital to risk-weighted assets ratio as of July 2024 [C067]. Following a Q1 2024 decline from Basel II adoption, CBS engaged banks to increase capital adequacy ratio (CAR) buffers through capital planning, yielding improvements in Q2 2024 [C067]. 

Liquidity remains robust, with commercial banks staying liquid and all banks keeping liquid asset to total liabilities ratios well above the 20 percent minimum requirement [C011], [C068]. 

However, non-performing loans (NPLs) remain elevated [C067]. Total NPLs rose 5.7 percent year-on-year to R852 million, though NPLs to gross loans fell to 7.2 percent by mid-2024 [C011], [C067].
